title: Sunday
summary: An everyday name, an old calendar and a delicious-sounding distraction.
question: Where did Sunday get its name?
completion: Sunday keeps an older English Sun-day name, translating a Roman calendar idea. German Sonntag is a cousin. Italian domenica follows a Lord’s-day name; the dessert word sundae is much newer.
partner: A similar sound is a clue. Let’s check the evidence.

evidence.title: A word on an old calendar
evidence.text: Sunne meant Sun and dæg meant day. Sunday developed from this Old English calendar name. It was already in use centuries before the ice-cream word sundae.

evidence.title: A Roman calendar clue
evidence.text: Dies Solis meant the Sun’s day. The Germanic calendar translated the Roman naming idea using its own Sun and day words. The idea could travel while the sounds changed.
